Hi Aisha —

Thanks again for taking time this morning. Quick recap and two asks so we can size a clean proposal:

Recap
- Use case: customer service automation + claims triage (short prompts, high QPS).
- Expected monthly active users: ~150K; estimated average 25 tokens per interaction (prompt + gen).
- Peak concurrency expected during EMEA morning windows (we discussed routing options).

Asks
1) Can you confirm ballpark monthly token volume (1M tokens/month, 10M, 100M, etc)? Even a 3-band estimate helps our pricing math.
2) What procurement threshold or approval band should we aim for (e.g., procurement requires SOW > $50k, finance requires PO > $100k)?

Based on the rough numbers we discussed, we want to validate a target unit economics number headlined as $/1M tokens so the procurement team understands the spend band. I attached a simple pricing sheet and a draft SOW for reference.

Next steps
- If you can share the monthly token band and any procurement thresholds, I’ll send a tailored pricing range and a one-page MRP (mutual action plan) with timelines.

Thanks —
Marissa

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A couple of clarifications from procurement finance side:

- Token volume: Our initial estimate for the first 6 months is roughly 50M–120M tokens/month (we see big variance during campaigns).
- Procurement thresholds: For vendor spend: approvals are as follows —
  - Up to $25k/month: local product manager sign-off
  - $25k–$100k/month: procurement + finance approval (standard PO)
  - > $100k/month: exec procurement + legal review, may require SOW and 60-day payment terms approval

We can be flexible on pilot size; if you can give us a target $/1M tokens range that maps to those bands, procurement can pre-clear the appropriate approvers.

Thanks,

Aisha —

Appreciate the breakdown. For budget math: a couple quick notes from our side that I'll include in the pricing range Marissa sends:

- We model unit economics by $/1M tokens. Typical hosted API tiers for similar customers land between $40–$250 per 1M tokens depending on model family, quantization, and caching.
- For high QPS short-prompt use cases, you typically get better effective $/1M via batching and prefix caching; we’ll assume a conservative 25% efficiency improvement for production over raw generation counts.
- For pricing guidance against procurement bands: if we can keep target spend below $100k/month, the process avoids exec legal review and speeds procurement.

Happy to jump on a short call with procurement if helpful.

-Rishi
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Thanks Aisha — and thanks Rishi for the pricing context.

Aisha, based on the 50M–120M tokens/month band you shared and our efficiency assumptions, here are two practical spend bands to slot into procurement:

- Conservative pilot (50M tokens/mo): target ~ $1,500–$6,000 per month (targeting $30–$120 per 1M tokens depending on model selection and caching).
- Production scale (120M tokens/mo): target ~ $3,600–$14,400 per month (targeting $30–$120 per 1M tokens).

Note: those ranges include typical discounts for reserved capacity and small-volume pilots; if you plan to commit to a 12-month reserved capacity, we can push unit costs toward the lower end ($30/1M tokens).

Next steps
1) If procurement confirms they need the formal SOW for > $100k spend, we can prioritize legal review — otherwise a standard PO will work.
2) I’ll upload a one-page mutual action plan and a mid-market pricing sheet reflecting the three model tiers (base, optimized, dedicated).

If this looks right, I’ll convert to a short proposal and include the explicit $/1M tokens math so the FP&A folks can slot it into forecasts.

Best,
Marissa
